scenes.text: Researchers discovered a two‑step compliance trick that lifts agreement rates.
First they ask for something trivial, like a free sticker.
Then, moments later, they request a larger favor.
Your brain tags the first agreement as a self‑label.
That label creates subconscious pressure to stay consistent.
